top_jobs.job: When a site change or a new app quietly breaks tracking, help me catch it the same day, so I do not spend 3 weeks cutting ads that were working
top_jobs.metric: tracked purchases per platform divided by store orders, daily

top_jobs.job: When Meta and Google together claim more sales than the store made, help me see what each one really drove, so I do not scale on sales counted twice
top_jobs.metric: sum of platform-claimed revenue divided by store revenue, same window, monthly

top_jobs.job: When the ads look great but the store is not growing, help me see whether we are buying new customers or rebuying old ones, so spend goes to growth and not to people who would come back anyway
top_jobs.metric: share of orders from new customers, and cost per new customer from store orders, 28 day

top_jobs.job: When numbers disagree or move and nobody knows why, help me have one meaning, one source and one owner per number, fresh every morning, so the Monday meeting is spent deciding
top_jobs.metric: share of headline numbers that passed the freshness check this morning

jobs.job: Match tracked purchases to store orders every morning (Meta, Google Ads and GA4 purchases, each divided by store orders) against their 28 day range, and alert when one falls out
jobs.trigger: every morning at 8
steps: Pull yesterday's purchases from each platform and the store's orders
Divide each platform's count by store orders, on the same day and time zone
Compare each ratio with its 28 day range
When one falls out of range, alert with the platform, the size of the drop and the hour it started
A person places a test order to confirm before anyone changes ads
jobs.output: a morning line per platform: in range or out, with the start time of any break

watch.metric: tracked purchases per platform divided by store orders
watch.source: Shopify, Meta Ads, Google Ads and GA4

jobs.drives: ads cut for the wrong reason

jobs.job: Before any theme, checkout app or site change goes live, place a test order and check that view, add to cart, checkout and purchase each fire once, with the right value, on every platform
jobs.trigger: before every site launch or app install

inputs.need: a copy of the theme or a test store
a way to place test orders at no cost

steps: Write the checklist: events, platforms, value, currency, order id
Place a test order on the copy of the theme
Check each event fired once with the right value on Meta, Google Ads and GA4
Mark pass or fail, and hold the launch on any fail
After launch, repeat on the live site and cancel the test order
jobs.output: a pass or fail sheet for each launch

watch.metric: events passing the pre-launch check

jobs.job: Check Meta's purchase event quality each week: browser and server events counted once, match quality, and the value sent (net sales, not with tax and shipping)
jobs.trigger: weekly, and after any change to the pixel or checkout

inputs.need: Meta dataset quality and event counts
orders with net sales, tax and shipping split

steps: Pull event counts, the share counted twice, and match quality for purchase
Compare Meta purchase value with store net sales for the same orders
Flag double counts, low match quality, and value that includes tax or shipping
Write the fix for the person who owns tracking; ecomOS changes nothing in Meta
jobs.output: a weekly event quality line with fixes

watch.metric: Meta purchases divided by store orders, and match quality

jobs.drives: Meta bidding on the right buyers

jobs.job: Find why GA4 shows fewer orders than the store each week (consent banner, checkout on another domain, duplicate tags, staff and test orders, or bots) and write the fix list
jobs.trigger: weekly

inputs.need: GA4 purchases and sessions by day, device and browser
consent banner settings and change dates
staff and agency IP addresses, and test orders

steps: Divide GA4 purchases by store orders, by day, device and browser
Check the gap before and after any consent or checkout change
Match order ids to find purchases missing or counted twice
Filter out staff, agency, test traffic and bots, and recount
Write the fix list with an owner for each
jobs.output: a weekly gap table and a fix list

watch.metric: GA4 purchases divided by Shopify orders

jobs.drives: trust in channel and conversion reports

jobs.job: When tracking was broken, list the days it touched, the budget and creative decisions made in those days, and the true numbers from store orders, so the wrong calls can be reversed
jobs.trigger: after any tracking break

inputs.need: store orders and ad spend for those days
inputs.from: Shopify, Meta Ads and Google Ads

steps: Mark the first and last day of the break
List every budget, pause and creative decision made in those days
Recompute each campaign's results from store orders by link tag
Mark decisions that would change with the true numbers
Founder reviews the list and a person reverses the wrong calls
jobs.output: a break report: days, decisions to review, and the true numbers

watch.metric: decisions made during a tracking break that were reviewed

jobs.job: Each month add up the revenue every platform claims (Meta, Google, TikTok, email, affiliates) for the same window, and set it against store revenue to show how much is claimed twice
jobs.trigger: monthly, and before any budget change over 20 percent

inputs.from: TikTok Ads and the email tool

steps: Pull claimed revenue per platform for the same calendar window
Write down the attribution window each platform used
Divide the sum of claims by store revenue
Show which platforms claim most of the gap, and the orders more than one of them claim
jobs.output: a claim sheet: claimed revenue by platform, store revenue, and the over-claim ratio
jobs.next: feeds 22-07 (check a great week) and 21-12 (spend line)

watch.metric: sum of platform-claimed revenue divided by store revenue

jobs.job: Before doubling a campaign after one great week, match its claimed purchases to store orders by link tag and time, split new and returning buyers and codes used, and hold the raise if under 60 percent match
jobs.trigger: before any budget raise over 30 percent

inputs.need: the campaign's claimed purchases by day
orders with link tags, codes and customer history

steps: Pull the campaign's claimed purchases for 7 days
Match them to store orders by link tag and order time
Split matched orders into new and returning buyers, and note discount codes from other channels
Write the verdict: real, partly real, or not, and hold the raise below 60 percent match
jobs.output: a 1 line verdict per campaign: real, partly real, or not

watch.metric: platform purchases matched to store orders for the campaign

jobs.job: Check the agency's monthly report against the store: their revenue divided by store matched revenue, the window they used, and the numbers they left out, in a 1 page note
jobs.trigger: monthly, when the report arrives
steps: Read each number in the report and the window it uses
Rebuild the same numbers from store orders
Divide the agency's revenue by store matched revenue
List what the report leaves out: returns, new customer share, margin
Write a 1 page note the founder can send back
jobs.output: a 1 page note on the agency report

watch.metric: agency-reported revenue divided by store matched revenue
watch.source: agency report, ad platforms and Shopify

jobs.drives: trust, and fee talks with the agency

jobs.job: Run a holdout on brand search or retargeting: switch it off in a third of states for 3 weeks, compare store orders with the rest, and decide from the extra sales it really adds
jobs.trigger: once per channel every 6 months, when a channel claims over 20 percent of sales

inputs.from: Google Ads and Meta Ads (read only; a person makes the change)

inputs.need: approval of the test and the sales at risk

steps: Pick matched groups of states from 12 weeks of orders
Estimate the sales at risk, and the founder approves
A person switches the channel off in the test states for 3 weeks
Compare orders per state with the forecast from the control states
Write the extra sales per dollar and the decision, and log it in the ledger
jobs.output: a holdout readout: extra sales per dollar with a range, and a keep, cut or trim decision

watch.metric: extra sales from the holdout, per channel
watch.source: store orders in test and holdout states

jobs.drives: spend on sales we already had

jobs.job: Add a post-purchase question, where did you first hear about us, with 8 fixed answers, and count the answers each month next to what the trackers credit
jobs.trigger: once to set up, then monthly

inputs.need: a post-purchase survey on the thank you page
channels we run, for the answer list

steps: Write 8 answers from the channels we run, plus other with a text box
Put the question on the thank you page
Each month count answers by channel
Set survey share next to last click share by channel
Flag channels the trackers miss, such as podcasts or word of mouth
jobs.output: a monthly table: survey share against tracker share, by channel

watch.metric: share of orders answering the question, and answers by source

jobs.job: Audit every link in emails, SMS, bios, creator posts and affiliate pages for the right tracking tag, fix the broken ones, and publish one tag rule so direct and unknown orders fall
jobs.trigger: once, then monthly

inputs.need: links in email and SMS flows

steps: List every live link by channel
Check each for source, medium and campaign tags
Fix missing or wrong tags, and a person updates flows and bios
Publish the tag rule for the team and agencies
Recount orders with no known source a month later
jobs.output: a link audit with fixes, and one tag rule

watch.metric: share of orders with no known source

jobs.job: Measure how much Meta ads lift Amazon sales: set weekly Meta spend against Amazon orders and brand searches on Amazon, and read it through Amazon Attribution links or a regional Meta pause
jobs.trigger: each quarter, or before a big Meta cut

inputs.need: Amazon orders and brand search volume
inputs.from: Amazon Seller Central and Brand Analytics

inputs.need: Amazon Attribution tags on some ads

steps: Line up weekly Meta spend, Amazon orders and Amazon brand searches for 26 weeks
Tag a share of Meta ads with Amazon Attribution links
If the founder approves, a person pauses Meta in a few regions for 3 weeks
Estimate Amazon sales per Meta dollar, with a range
Write a rule for judging Meta with Amazon sales counted
jobs.output: a halo estimate with a range, and a rule for judging Meta

watch.metric: Amazon sales against Meta spend

jobs.drives: good ads cut for the wrong reason

jobs.job: Split every ad dollar and every order by funnel stage (prospecting or retargeting on Meta, generic or brand search on Google, new or returning buyer in the store) in one weekly table
jobs.trigger: every Monday
steps: Map each campaign to a stage, and a person checks the map once
Split spend by stage on each platform
Split orders into new and returning by customer history
Show the share of spend on prospecting and generic, and the share of orders from new customers, for 12 weeks
Write the 1 line answer: are we buying new customers or rebuying old ones
jobs.output: a weekly funnel mix table with 12 weeks of trend, and the 1 line answer

watch.metric: share of orders from new customers, and share of spend on prospecting
watch.source: Meta Ads, Google Ads and Shopify

jobs.job: Count new customers from store orders (first order ever, by email or phone), set that against what Meta and Google call new, and publish one cost per new customer
jobs.trigger: monthly

inputs.need: new customer counts the platforms claim

steps: Define new: first order ever, by email or phone, across all channels
Count new customers per month from the store
Compare with each platform's claim, and list the gap
Cost per new customer = total ad spend divided by store new customers, from totals
Write the meaning into the metric contract
jobs.output: one cost per new customer, with the gap to platform claims
jobs.next: feeds 21-13 (payback) and 15-19 (Meta buyers who already bought)

watch.metric: new customers from store orders against platform claims

jobs.job: Measure brand search inflation: the share of Google spend and conversions on brand terms, the share of those buyers who already bought, and what brand ads add that organic results would not
jobs.trigger: monthly

inputs.need: orders with Google click ids and customer history

steps: Split Google spend and conversions into brand and generic terms
Match brand search orders to customer history: new or returning
Set brand paid clicks next to brand organic clicks over 12 weeks
Write keep, trim or test, and send a test to 22-09 when brand spend is large
jobs.output: a brand search table and a keep, trim or test note

watch.metric: share of Google conversions on brand terms from returning buyers

jobs.drives: spend on buyers who would come anyway

jobs.job: Watch 90 day repeat rate by first order month and new customers per week side by side, and flag when either falls 2 months in a row
jobs.trigger: monthly

inputs.need: orders with first order month per customer

steps: Compute 90 day repeat rate for each first order month
Count new customers per week and cost per new customer
Put both on one chart for 12 months
Flag when either falls 2 months in a row, and send the flag to the right screen
jobs.output: a pair of trend lines and a flag

watch.metric: 90 day repeat rate by first order month

jobs.job: Write the metric contract for the top 15 numbers (name, meaning, formula, source, window, owner, and what shows when data is missing), fold marketplace and wholesale sales into total sales, and have the founder sign it
jobs.trigger: once, then when a number is added or disputed

inputs.need: the numbers used in today's reports and meetings
metric rules already written for the app
revenue outside the store and where it lives

steps: List the 15 numbers the team uses most
Write one meaning, formula, source, window and owner for each
Add sales from marketplaces and wholesale as their own source, so total sales counts every channel
Write what shows when a source is missing: unavailable, never zero
Founder signs, and every report links each number to the contract
jobs.output: a signed contract of 15 numbers

watch.metric: minutes of the weekly meeting spent on which number is right

jobs.job: Check every feed each morning before the report goes out (last sync time, row counts against normal, missing days and time zone) and stamp each headline number fresh or stale
jobs.trigger: every morning, before the report

inputs.need: sync logs for the store, ad platforms and GA4
sync log for the email tool
time zone and currency per tool

steps: Read the last sync time and row count for each feed
Compare row counts with the normal range, and look for missing days
Check each tool's day ends at the same hour as the store's
Stamp each headline number fresh or stale, with the reason
Send stale feeds to the person who owns them
jobs.output: a freshness strip on each report

watch.metric: share of headline numbers that passed the freshness check

jobs.drives: acting on half a day of data

jobs.job: Keep a change log of every theme publish, app install, tag edit, price change and campaign restructure with the date, and when a number shifts, list what changed that day
jobs.trigger: on every change, read when a number moves

inputs.from: Meta Ads and Google Ads (read only)

inputs.need: changes the team makes by hand

steps: Pull changes from each connected account every day
Add hand entries from the team through the work board
Keep one dated list with who made each change
When a number shifts, list every change in the 48 hours before
jobs.output: a dated change log, and a what-changed list for any shift

watch.metric: hours to find the cause of a number shift

jobs.job: When revenue drops, split the change into visits, buy rate and order size by channel and device, check stock and late returns, and name the part that moved in 1 line
jobs.trigger: when daily revenue moves 15 percent against the same day last week

inputs.need: in-stock share of top page sizes and colours

steps: Split the revenue change into visits, buy rate and order size
Split each by channel and device, and find the biggest mover
Check the funnel step that moved: product view, cart, or checkout
Check stock on top pages, and returns landing from last month's sale
Check the change log for that day, then write the 1 line cause and an owner
jobs.output: a 1 line cause with the numbers behind it, and an owner

watch.metric: change in revenue split into visits, buy rate and order size

new_enablers.name: Tracking and claim check
new_enablers.what: Every morning matches each platform's purchases and revenue (Meta, Google, TikTok, GA4, email) to store orders, checks event health (fires once, right value, match quality), and shows how much each platform claims against what the store sold.
powers: same day alert on a tracking break
verdict on a great week before scaling

new_enablers.name: Metric contract and data health
new_enablers.what: One meaning, formula, source, window, owner and missing-data rule for each headline number. A freshness stamp per feed each morning, a dated change log of site, app, tag and account changes, and the split of any move into visits, buy rate and order size.
powers: fresh or stale stamps on reports
the cause of a shift in minutes

new_enablers.name: Holdout test kit
new_enablers.what: Designs and reads tests that switch a channel off for part of the country or part of the audience for 2 to 4 weeks, and measures store orders against the rest. Tells what a channel adds, not what it claims. A person makes every account change.
inputs: founder approval of the sales at risk
powers: extra sales per dollar per channel
